Jay Leno Gets Up Close and Personal With Hennessey Blackbird: Zero Screens and No Electrification
14 photos
Photo: Jay Leno's Garage | YouTube
Meet the 2029 Hennessey Blackbird before you are actually supposed to meet it. The Blackbird is the upcoming, ultra-exclusive, all-analog hypercar, designed as an act of rebellion against modern electrified vehicles with cabins covered in screens. This is the car that Jay Leno now gets up close and personal with long before deliveries even start.
Jay Leno and John Hennessey have a history together. They first met back in 1993. At the time, John was a hot rodder who turned Dodge Vipers into venomous machines. Since then, he has built three insane hypercars. First came the Hennessey Venom GT with 1,244 horsepower (1,261 metric horsepower). A decade later, he came up with the Venom F5 in standard form, boasting 1,817 horsepower (1,842 metric horsepower).
In January 2026, the Venom F5 Evolution broke cover with a mind-blowing 2,031 horsepower (2,059 metric horsepower). Now, he has come up with the Blackbird, which is unlike any car he has built before. It comes with the most powerful naturally aspirated V8 ever put in a road-going production car.
But with no supercharger, turbocharger, or electrification, the Hennessey Blackbir d is more about the driver than about speed and horsepower. It is unlike anything John Hennessey has ever built and something that nobody would expect from him.
Photo: Jay Leno's Garage | YouTube Nathan Malinick , head of design at Hennessey, brought an SR-71 Blackbird prototype to Jay Leno’s Garage to tell the story that has just begun. The 2029 Hennessey Blackbird was officially unveiled during the Monterey Car Week in August 2026 under the codename "Project Overlord."
The hypercar trades straight-line performance for absolute driver engagement, drawing inspiration from the legendary Lockheed SR-71 Blackbird reconnaissance aircraft. There is a crease stretching along the side pod, imitating the plane’s chine line.
The diamond-shaped headlights are actually inspired by the inlet spikes on the front of the SR-71 Blackbird's engines, which moved back and forth to control airflow at supersonic speeds, while the rear lights mimic the glowing afterburners of the jet. The quad-exhaust array at the rear of the Hennessey Blackbird is directly inspired by the four rocket nozzles on Chuck Yeager's Bell X-1.
The Blackbird rides on lightweight forged wheels, measuring 20 inches up front and 21 inches out back, wrapped in off-the-shelf Michelin Pilot Sport Cup 2 tires with nothing custom about them. Brembo carbon ceramic brakes provide the stopping power.
Photo: Jay Leno's Garage | YouTube Developed in partnership with Ilmor Engineering, the engine that powers it is somewhat of a masterpiece: a high-revving, mid-mounted 6.2-liter V8 with naturally aspirated firepower, with a target output between 800 and 850 horsepower, redlining at an incredible 9,000 rpm.
A six-speed gated manual transmission sends power to the ground through the rear wheels. Who would have thought there would still be manual cars in 2029? The model is expected to hit 60 mph (97 kph) from a standstill in 2.5 seconds and max out at 220 mph (354 kph).
Sure, there are hypercars out there that come with more than 850 horsepower, but not many of them sport such a lightweight architecture. The Blackbird is built completely from a carbon fiber monocoque tub and carbon body panels. That is why it tips the scales at under 3,000 pounds (1,361 kilograms).
The Hennessey-badged model features aerospace-inspired active vertical stabilizers that automatically deploy at 71 mph (114 kph) at an angle of 71 degrees. “That is the Blackbird flying,” Nathan Malinick explains.
Photo: Jay Leno's Garage | YouTube The doors of the prototype that was parked in Jay Leno’s Garage don’t open. But when they do, they will be dihedral synchro-helix or butterfly-style doors, providing access to a cabin that completely rejects digital trends. The dashboard is entirely screenless in an era in which automakers are struggling to offer the largest screen surface on board their vehicles. Instead, it features five traditional analog dials and a large central tachometer.
Because the car has a solid rear bulkhead and an engine cover that blocks the view out the back window, an actual rearview mirror would be useless. However, to get around this while staying legal for road use, Hennessey uses a digital rearview mirror. There is a camera on the back, streaming a live, high-definition video onto a hidden display built inside the glass of the rearview mirror.
An exposed manual shift linkage, physical switches, and a completely buttonless steering wheel are also on the menu, along with a classic ignition key and a roof-mounted start button. The cabin also hosts a mechanical whiskey compass, the type used in early aviation and marine navigation for those moments when the driver has no Google Maps or Waze available.
Photo: Jay Leno's Garage | YouTube It is called a "whiskey" compass because the glass bowl housing the magnetic card is filled with a clear fluid, an alcohol-water mix like whiskey or pure ethanol to dampen vibrations and stop the compass needle from swinging wildly.
Instead of a digital clock, the Hennessey Blackbird will come with a removable dash-top timepiece with a high-end luxury mechanical design, styled after the aircraft chronometers from the mid-20th century, which pilots used to time flight legs. The clock features a quick-release mechanism, so that the driver can unlock it from the dashboard dock and wear it as a wristwatch or place it into a desk stand when they are done driving.
The Blackbird has also been designed with practicality in mind. The front trunk is specifically sized to fit two airline-approved carry-on flight cases, because the car was designed with the wives in mind, says Nathan. There is also an integrated luggage space behind the front seats, alongside unique exterior saddlebag compartments built into the lifting rear quarter panels. It sounds like it’s got the most luggage space of all hypercars.
Hennessey will only build 71 units, each starting at an eye-watering $2.5 million . Customer deliveries are scheduled to kick off in 2029.
